items.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25
items.q: When we started that band, we had Willie Jones, that little brother, got killed by an automobile.

ctx.x: That's my argument with him. I'm trying to convince him that you don't have to stop playing music to go to the church. He seems to think you have to do one or the other to go to church or play the music.

So I'm about to win him over, I think, on that. All them girls always tell me. One time I'd say, yeah, there's a church right across the street in the house. I bet you ain't never been there yet. I'd go to church, playing that music. I'd say, that's all right. I'd say, God give me that gift. I had one that tell me, I let them call and say, God going to knock me down one day at the drum. He ain't knocked me down yet, and she's out there in the Hope Cemetery, and I'm still there. She was going to church.…

Willie Jones was one of the great, great Clannett brothers. I don't know if you knew him. I know his brother. I know John. John, yeah. John, I played with John. Well I played with John too. Yeah, but I'm talking about the one that John's playing. I'm trying to get him in this outfit that I'm getting together now on the bass. Well I take a few lessons from his brother Willie. Yeah, he's good. And he was a real good drunk man. Well voiced on music. Yeah, read music. Read real good.
